newsitem.title: USA: Ex-soldier guilty of N.Carolina race murders.
newsitem.headline: Ex-soldier guilty of N.Carolina race murders.

text.p: A former U.S. Army paratrooper linked to a white supremacist group was found guilty on Thursday of murdering a black couple in a racially motivated slaying in 1995.
James Burmeister, 21, was convicted of two counts of first-degree murder for the deaths of Jackie Burden, 27, and Michael James, 36. First-degree murder requires premeditation.

The couple were shot at close range as they walked through a Fayetteville neighbourhood in December 1995. During the trial, prosecutor John Dickson told jurors Burmeister personified "pure, unmitigated evil" because he killed the couple out of racial hatred.

Burmeister, who was serving in the Army's elite 82nd Airborne Division at Fort Bragg, which adjoins Fayetteville, had been drinking beer with fellow soldiers Randy Meadows and Malcolm Wright before the murders.

The penalty phase, where prosecutors will ask the jury to sentence Burmeister to death, was to get underway later in the day. A life sentence would make Burmeister eligible for parole after serving 25 years.
Burmeister, of Thompson, Pennsylvania, was also found guilty of conspiracy to commit murder. He showed no emotion as the verdicts were read.

Meadows, 22, of Mulkeytown, Illinois, testified that after leaving the bar he drove Burmeister and Wright, 22, to the area where the couple were killed. He said he heard six gunshots after Burmeister and Wright got out of the car.

Dickson said Burmeister wanted to earn a "spider web" tattoo, a skinhead symbol police say represents the killing of a gay or black person. White supremacist and bomb-making literature and a Nazi flag were found at Burmeister's trailer.
Defence lawyers argued that Burmeister had consumed nearly two gallons (7.6 litres) of beer and was too drunk to form the intent to kill.
